intent: To explore the potential changes or scenarios required to increase public transit usage by reducing the dominance of driving alone.

units.meaning: Public transportation accounts for 5.2% of commuters in the baseline pie.
accepted_routes: Public transit makes up about 5% (one in twenty) of the chart.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Public transportation slice must be labeled or directly annotated with 5.2% (or clearly rounded to 5%).
units.temporal_anchor: The narration clause asking about getting more Americans to use public transit.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state the baseline public transit share before proposing any increase?

units.meaning: Drive alone is the largest commute mode, at 76.3%.
accepted_routes: About three in four commuters drive alone.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Drive-alone slice must be visually dominant and labeled/annotated with 76.3% (or clearly rounded to 76%).
units.temporal_anchor: The narration clause about reducing the dominance of driving alone / shrinking this part of the chart.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly identify drive alone as the largest mode and give its 76.3% share?

units.meaning: The drive-alone share exceeds public transportation by 71.1 percentage points, and is about 14.7 times the public transit share.
units.computation: difference = 76.3 - 5.2 = 71.1 percentage points; ratio = 76.3 / 5.2 ≈ 14.67, rounded to 14.7
accepted_routes: Drive alone is 71.1 points higher than public transit.
The gap is about 71 percentage points.
Drive alone is nearly 15 times public transit (76.3% vs 5.2%).
Drive alone is more than 14 times public transit.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A direct comparison or callout must relate the 76.3% drive-alone slice to the 5.2% public-transit slice; exact ratio may be shown or stated.
units.temporal_anchor: The narration clause contrasting public transit with the dominant drive-alone share.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video quantify the drive-alone/public-transit gap or ratio, or is showing both shares enough?

optional_valid: Carpool is the second-largest mode at 8.2%.
Work at home is 5.1%, nearly tied with public transportation at 5.2%.
Bicycle is the smallest mode at 1.0%.
unsupported_to_avoid: Do not claim that a specific scenario, such as a given percentage shift from driving to transit, is in the data; no target or policy effect is provided.
Do not say reducing drive-alone causes public transit to rise by a specific amount unless framed as hypothetical and not attributed to the table.
Do not claim public transit is the second-largest mode; carpool is 8.2%, larger than public transit at 5.2%.
Do not use a wrong denominator or compare to all Americans rather than the commute-mode pie.
Do not extrapolate that drive-alone can be shrunk to a specific percentage; the table only gives baseline shares.
notes: The core baseline is a 100% commute-mode pie where drive alone is 76.3% and public transit is 5.2%; any 'what would it take' must be framed as a hypothetical because the table has no scenario targets. Optional context includes mode ranking and combined shares.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
